The season started on 28 August 2018 and concluded on 15 May 2019.{{Cite news |title=المسابقات تعلن عن جدول دوري الأمير محمد بن سلمان|url=https://www.dawriplus.com/news/31874-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%85%D8%B3%D8%A7%D8%A8%D9%82%D8%A7%D8%AA-%D8%AA%D8%B9%D9%84%D9%86-%D8%B9%D9%86-%D8%AC%D8%AF%D9%88%D9%84-%D8%AF%D9%88%D8%B1%D9%8A-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A3%D9%85%D9%8A%D8%B1-%D9%85%D8%AD%D9%85%D8%AF-%D8%A8%D9%86-%D8%B3%D9%84%D9%85%D8%A7%D9%86.html|date=25 July 2018|accessdate=11 September 2018}} Fixtures for the 2018–19 season were announced on 25 July 2018. The first team to be promoted was [[Abha Club|Abha]], following their 2–2 draw away to [[Al-Nojoom FC|Al-Nojoom]] on 30 April 2019.{{cite web |title=أبها يعود إلى دوري المحترفين بعد غياب 10 أعوام|date=30 April 2019|url=https://www.alwatan.com.sa/article/1007843/%D8%B1%D9%8A%D8%A7%D8%B6%D8%A9/%D8%B3%D8%B9%D9%88%D8%AF%D9%8A%D8%A9/%D8%A3%D8%A8%D9%87%D8%A7-%D9%8A%D8%B9%D9%88%D8%AF-%D8%A5%D9%84%D9%89-%D8%AF%D9%88%D8%B1%D9%8A-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%85%D8%AD%D8%AA%D8%B1%D9%81%D9%8A%D9%86-%D8%A8%D8%B9%D8%AF-%D8%BA%D9%8A%D8%A7%D8%A8-10-%D8%A3%D8%B9%D9%88%D8%A7%D9%85}} Division rebranding=== On 7 March 2018, the Saudi FF announced that the league would be increased from 16 teams to 20 teams.{{cite web|title=تنفيذاً لقرار مجلس ادارة الاتحاد السعودي لكرة القدم بزيادة عدد الأندية في الموسم المقبل|url=https://twitter.com/saudiFF/status/971360307330338817|language=Arabic|publisher=[[Saudi Arabian Football Federation|SAFF]]|date=7 March 2018|accessdate=7 March 2018}} The competition will be known as the Prince [[Mohammad bin Salman]] League for the second season.{{cite web |website= Twitter.com |url=https://twitter.com/Turki_alalshikh/status/961929088201056256|title= إطلاق اسم سيدي ولي العهد على دوري الدرجة الأولى ليصبح|publisher=gsa |date=9 February 2018}} ===Rule changes=== On 7 March 2018, the SAFF announced that the numbers of foreign players were increased from 3 players to 7 players. They also increased the prize money to SAR 10 million.{{cite web |url=https://www.okaz.com.sa/article/1617980/%D8%B1%D9%8A%D8%A7%D8%B6%D8%A9/10-%D9%85%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%8A%D9%8A%D9%86-%D9%887-%D8%A3%D8%AC%D8%A7%D9%86%D8%A8-%D9%81%D9%8A-%D8%AF%D9%88%D8%B1%D9%8A-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A3%D9%85%D9%8A%D8%B1-%D9%85%D8%AD%D9%85%D8%AF-%D8%A8%D9%86-%D8%B3%D9%84%D9%85%D8%A7%D9%86|title=10 ملايين و7 أجانب في دوري الأمير محمد بن سلمان|date=24 February 2018 |accessdate= 11 September 2018}} ==Teams== A total of 20 teams are contesting the league, including 9 sides from the [[2017–18 Prince Mohammad bin Salman League|2017–18 season]], 6 promoted teams from the [[2017–18 Saudi Second Division|Second Division]], the two playoff losers from the [[2017–18 Saudi Professional League#Relegation play-offs|2017–18 Pro League playoffs]], and three winners from the [[2017–18 Prince Mohammad bin Salman League#Relegation play-offs|2017–18 relegation playoffs]]. No teams were relegated from the Pro League. Due to an increase in the number of teams, the Saudi FF announced that the relegation was canceled and in its place was a relegation play-off. Both Pro League teams, [[Al-Raed FC|Al-Raed]] and [[Ohod Club|Ohod]], won the playoffs and secured their top-flight status. [[Al-Washm Club|Al-Washm]] were promoted as the winners of the [[2017–18 Saudi Second Division|Second Division]] and [[Al-Jabalain FC|Al-Jabalain]] were promoted as the runners-up. [[Al Jeel Club|Al-Jeel]] defeated [[Al-Ansar FC (Medina)|Al-Ansar]] in the third place playoffs. Both teams were promoted after the increase of teams. The 4 teams were joined by the third-placed teams of both groups, [[Al-Adalah FC|Al-Adalah]] and [[Al-Ain FC (Saudi football club)|Al-Ain]]. [[Abha Club|Abha]] defeated [[Al-Watani]] in the relegation playoffs and became the only Second Division side to win their relegation playoff match. Al-Washm and Al-Ain will play in the [[Prince Mohammad bin Salman League]] for the first time in their history. Al-Jabalain return to the MS League for the first time since the 2007–08 season. Abha return to the MS League for the first time since the [[2014–15 Saudi First Division|2014–15 season]]. Al-Ansar return to the MS League for the first time since the [[2013–14 Saudi First Division|2013–14 season]]. Al-Adalah and Al-Jeel return to the MS League after only a season's absence. On 4 May 2018 [[Al-Watani]] became the only club to be relegated to the Second Division following their 1–0 defeat to [[Abha Club|Abha]].{{cite web |url=https://www.spa.gov.sa/1759653|title=فريق أبها يصعد لدوري الأمير محمد بن سلمان|date=4 May 2018 |accessdate= 11 September 2018}} ==Team changes== The following teams have changed division since the 2017–18 season. {{col-begin}} {{col-2}} ===To Prince Mohammad bin Salman League=== '''Promoted from [[2017–18 Saudi Second Division|Second Division]]''' * [[Al-Washm Club|Al-Washm]] * [[Al-Jabalain FC|Al-Jabalain]] * [[Al Jeel Club|Al-Jeel]] * [[Al-Ansar FC (Medina)|Al-Ansar]] * [[Al-Ain FC (Saudi football club)|Al-Ain]] * [[Al-Adalah FC|Al-Adalah]] * [[Abha Club|Abha]] ===From Prince Mohammad bin Salman League=== '''Promoted to [[2018–19 Saudi Professional League|Pro League]]''' * [[Al-Wehda Club (Mecca)|Al-Wehda]] * [[Al-Hazem F.C.|Al-Hazem]] '''Relegated to [[2018–19 Saudi Second Division|Second Division]]''' * [[Al-Watani]] {{col-end}} ==Stadia and locations==
